x-draft: ADR-0036 (proposed): written by homelabnext.novelty (hnx novelty run) and read by its corroborate; not frozen until ADR-0036 is accepted
title: Novelty Finding
description: An advisory behavioural-novelty finding (ADR-0036 decision 6; docs/novelty.md): the platform's own table in the OCSF conventions of this directory, not an OCSF class (ocsf_class_uid 0 is OCSF's base event). Every row is heuristic: no deterministic gate escalates on one alone. Written by the lake novelty analyzer and, in the same shape, by host-kernel sensors with their own source.

uid.description: Deterministic id within its source: a digest of the source, the profile's spec, as_of, status, entity kind, entity and value. With source, the idempotency (content) key of the table, so one source cannot claim another's uid.

time.description: The start of the behaviour window the finding describes: score_since for the lake analyzer (as_of - score_hours), the observation time for a host sensor. corroborate windows on it. RFC 3339 with an explicit offset; stored as UTC.

as_of.description: The instant the run scored up to (the end of the scoring window).

source.description: What produced the finding: lake-novelty for the lake analyzer, a host sensor's own name otherwise. A cooperating writer writes only its own source (write_findings checks the rows, the mark and the batch id; the lake refuses another source's batch id), so distinct sources are distinct writers; the engine cannot check which source an inserted row names, so this is a convention of the writers, not a guarantee. corroborate counts distinct sources.

source_kind.description: Always heuristic: a novelty finding is advisory (ADR-0036 decision 6).

profile.description: The spec profile (or the host sensor's baseline) that produced the finding.

entity_kind.description: The shared entity namespace the entity belongs to (ADR-0036 decision 7): every source names an address as ip, a host as host and so on, so corroborate matches one entity across sources by (entity_kind, entity), never by bare text.

entity.description: The entity's value as text (a string as is, anything else as JSON).

entity_column.description: The column path the entity came from.

value.description: The value as text: the one value, or a JSON array when the profile has several value columns. Absent for a burst or high-cardinality row.

value_columns.description: The column paths the value came from.

status.description: finding: scored at or above emit_at; unlearned: the entity has no learned support, so no score; burst: more distinct values than the profile allows in the scoring window alone (a scan), reported once with its row count there, not scored, and a signal; high_cardinality: more distinct learned values than the profile allows, reported once and not scored, not a signal.

score.description: surprise x confidence; present only when status is finding.

confidence.description: min(1, entity_total / entity_min_samples); present only when status is finding.

support.description: Decayed support s(entity, value) in the learning window.

entity_total.description: Decayed entity total T(entity) over all its values in the learning window.

count.description: Rows of (entity, value) in the scoring window.

learn_until.description: End of the learning window (exclusive) = start of the scoring window.

score_until.description: End of the scoring window (exclusive) = as_of.

spec_digest.description: sha256 of the profile's canonical spec, so a finding names the parameters that produced it.

message.description: One line: what is new, for whom, and the arithmetic.

reasons.description: The terms of the decision, one per entry (support, total, surprise, confidence, threshold).

tlp.description: The row's TLP 2.0 label (ADR-0033 decision 5): the strictest label among the rows that produced the finding, its learning-window rows included (ADR-0036 decision 5). The lake refuses a row without one.
